title: Dual Koszul cohomology below the top degree
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $r\in\mathbb N$, and $f:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A$ a Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Let $K^\vee$ be its signed dual cochain Koszul complex [def-sc-koszul-dual-complex]. For every $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n<r$, the module $H^n(K^\vee)$ is zero.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ, lemma-regular-immersion-ext, local signed dual Koszul computation; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BQZ

proof.text: For the ordered standard basis of E=A^r, send the dual of each n-element ordered basis wedge to its complementary (r-n)-element wedge with the permutation sign. These give linear isomorphisms in degrees 0 through r. Evaluate the contraction differential on basis wedges; the signed dual differential corresponds to the reversed contraction differential up to a degree-dependent sign. Starting with sign 1 in degree zero, rescale recursively by unit signs so each differential square commutes. Terms beyond r vanish by the exterior-power basis.

Transport degree-n cohomology along these isomorphisms. It is degree-(r-n) homology of the original Koszul complex. Since n<r, this index is positive and Koszul-regularity makes it zero. When r=0 no such n exists; the construction remains valid over the zero ring.
